Fit a Mixed Markov Model

Source: R/mmm.R
build_mmm.Rd

build_mmm() fits a mixture of first-order Markov chains to a set of sequences by expectation-maximisation: it looks for k subgroups whose members move between states in different ways, each with its own transition matrix and initial-state distribution. Every sequence gets a posterior probability of belonging to each subgroup and is assigned to the most probable one. Covariates can shape the mixing proportions during estimation or be related to the subgroups afterwards (see covariate_effect).

EM finds a local maximum, so the fit is started n_starts times (one start from k-means on the transition counts, the rest random), each is screened with a short EM run, the most promising are continued for up to max_iter iterations, and the one with the highest log-likelihood is kept. print() reports whether it converged within max_iter; a fit that did not is not a result. The information criteria (BIC, AIC, ICL) compare fits with different k – compare_mmm() fits a range of them – while average posterior probability (AvePP), entropy and classification error describe how cleanly the sequences separate within one fit. None of them picks k alone: also check that the subgroups' transition matrices differ in ways that can be interpreted, and that each subgroup holds enough sequences to estimate its matrix.

Usage

build_mmm(
  data,
  k = 2L,
  n_starts = 50L,
  max_iter = 200L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  smooth = 0.01,
  seed = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  covariate_effect = c("em", "posthoc"),
  estimator = c("auto", "firth", "multinom", "chisq")
)

# S3 method for class 'net_mmm'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mmm'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mmm'
plot(x, type = c("posterior", "covariates"), combined = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mmm_clustering'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mmm_clustering'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("posterior", "covariates", "predictors"),
  combined = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The sequences: a data frame with one row per sequence and one column per position, a netobject or bare cograph_network built from sequences, or a tna model (whose stored states are decoded to their labels). Columns take the same roles as in build_network(): an id or a covariate is not a position, and the columns set aside are named in a message and kept as metadata. Association networks (cor, pcor, glasso, ising, mgm) hold variables, not sequences, and raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

k

The number of subgroups (mixture components), a whole number of at least 2. Default 2.

n_starts

How many starting configurations to try, a positive whole number. More starts make it likelier that the best local maximum is found. Default 50.

max_iter

The most EM iterations a start may run, a positive whole number. Default 200.

tol

The convergence tolerance: EM stops when the log-likelihood changes by less than this between iterations (with covariate_effect = "em", also when its relative change does). A finite positive number; default 1e-6.

smooth

A pseudo-count added to every transition count before the matrices are estimated, so a transition unseen in a subgroup gets a small probability instead of zero. A finite non-negative number; default 0.01.

seed

An integer that makes the random starts reproducible. Default NULL. The session's own random stream is left as it was.

covariates

Variables describing each sequence (such as a course or a grade), given as a column name, a character vector of names, a one-sided formula or a data frame, as in build_clusters(). For a netobject, names are looked up in its metadata first, so a typical call is build_mmm(net, k = 3, covariates = "session_label"). How they enter the model is set by covariate_effect. Default NULL.

covariate_effect

How covariates enter the model. "em" (default) makes the mixing proportions depend on them during EM, so they shape the subgroups found and add (k - 1) * p parameters for p covariate columns; rows with a missing covariate are dropped first, with a warning. "posthoc" fits a plain mixture on every sequence and relates the covariates to the subgroups only afterwards, with a multinomial logit, so neither their values nor their missingness change the subgroups. Ignored without covariates.

estimator

How the after-fit multinomial logit is estimated; it never affects the EM. "auto" (default) uses Firth's penalised likelihood (brglm2::brmultinom(), finite under separation) when a cell of the subgroup-by-covariate table has fewer than 5 sequences, and nnet::multinom() otherwise. "firth" and "multinom" force one of them ("multinom" warns about separation risk), and "chisq" runs descriptive tests instead of a logit. build_clusters() has the details. Ignored without covariates.

x

For the print() and plot() methods: a net_mmm fit, or the net_mmm_clustering attribute of the netobject_group built from one.

digits

For the print() methods: decimal places of the statistics. Default 3.

...

For the print(), summary() and plot() methods: not used; any extra argument raises an error.

object

For the summary() method: a net_mmm fit.

type

For the plot() methods: "posterior" (default), a histogram of each sequence's largest posterior probability, coloured by cluster; or "covariates", a forest plot of the covariate effects, for a model fitted with covariates. On a net_mmm_clustering, "predictors" is an alias of "covariates".

combined

For the plot() methods with type = "covariates": TRUE (default) draws the forest panels as one faceted plot; FALSE returns a list of ggplots, one per cluster.

Value

A net_mmm object. print() shows the fit statistics, classification quality and subgroup sizes; summary() adds each subgroup's transition matrix and returns one row per subgroup (mixing proportion, sequences assigned, mean posterior, AvePP); plot() draws the posterior probabilities or the covariate effects; build_network() turns the fit into one network per subgroup (a netobject_group); cluster_diagnostics() and session_ids() give the classification and each sequence's subgroup. The object's fields:

data

The full N-row sequence frame used for estimation.

models

List of netobjects, one per component. Each component carries the rows assigned to that component in its $data slot, while its transition matrix is the EM-estimated component transition matrix.

k

Number of components.

mixing

Numeric vector of mixing proportions.

posterior

N x k matrix of posterior probabilities.

assignments

Integer vector of hard assignments (1..k).

quality

List: avepp (per-class), avepp_overall, entropy, relative_entropy, classification_error, class_entropy.

log_likelihood, BIC, AIC, ICL

Model fit statistics.

n_params

Number of free parameters behind BIC/AIC/ICL. With covariate_effect = "em" it grows by (k - 1) * p for p covariate columns.

iterations, converged

EM iterations used by the retained fit and whether it met tol.

states

Character vector of state names.

n_sequences

Number of sequences actually fitted (rows with missing covariates are dropped under covariate_effect = "em").

covariates

The post-hoc covariate analysis (list), or NULL when covariates = NULL.

network_method, build_args, htna_partition

Provenance kept from netobject / HTNA input so per-cluster networks can be rebuilt the same way; NULL otherwise.

metadata

The netobject's per-sequence metadata, one row per fitted sequence in the row order of posterior, so session_ids can name each sequence; NULL for other input.

The print() methods return their input invisibly. For a model fitted with covariates, summary() also prints the covariate profiles and effects and returns, invisibly, a tidy_covariates data frame of the effects (one row per subgroup other than the reference and per predictor term, so a factor gives one row per non-reference level; one row per covariate test with estimator = "chisq"), with the per-subgroup table as its cluster_stats attribute. The plot() methods print the plot and return the ggplot invisibly; with type = "covariates" and combined = FALSE they return, invisibly and without printing, a list of ggplots named by subgroup.

Initial states

Each sequence's initial state is the value in its first position column, read as it is: the function does not look ahead to the first observed state, and it does not convert missing-value symbols as build_clusters() does. The states are the distinct non-missing values of all position columns, so a placeholder such as "*" or "%" for an empty cell becomes a state, and a sequence starting with it starts in that state. Recode such placeholders to NA first: a missing first position gives the sequence no initial state, which leaves its subgroup to the transitions alone. Or trim leading empty cells so every first position holds an observed state.

A one-hot network is different: its units are windows of codes, not positions, so its initial state is the one code active in the first window, and none when that window holds several codes or none.

Methods

print() of a net_mmm shows a header with the numbers of sequences, subgroups and states, the log-likelihood and the information criteria; a quality line with the overall AvePP, the normalised entropy (0 when every sequence is classified with certainty, 1 when all posteriors are equal) and the classification error (the expected share of sequences misclassified when each is assigned to its most likely subgroup, the mean of one minus the largest posterior; Vermunt & Magidson, 2005); a line when the EM did not converge; and one row per subgroup with its size, mixing proportion and AvePP. For a model fitted with covariates, a last line names them, says whether they entered the EM (integrated) or were related post hoc, and gives their number. The layout follows print() of a net_clustering from build_clusters(), so dissimilarity-based and model-based clusterings read alike.

build_network() on a fit, and cluster_network() with cluster_by = "mmm", return a netobject_group whose "clustering" attribute is a net_mmm_clustering: the fit without its subgroup networks. Its print() shows the same quality line, information criteria and subgroup table, without the state count, the log-likelihood or the convergence line, and its plot() draws the same two views as plot() of a net_mmm. The "silhouette", "mds" and "heatmap" views of a dissimilarity-based clustering need a distance matrix, which an MMM clustering does not have, so asking for them raises an error.

References

Helske, S., & Helske, J. (2019). Mixture hidden Markov models for sequence data: The seqHMM package in R. Journal of Statistical Software, 88(3), 1–32. doi:10.18637/jss.v088.i03

Vermunt, J. K., & Magidson, J. (2005). Latent GOLD 4.0 User's Guide. Statistical Innovations.

See also

compare_mmm, build_network

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(V1 = sample(c("A","B","C"), 30, TRUE),
                   V2 = sample(c("A","B","C"), 30, TRUE))
mmm <- build_mmm(seqs, k = 2, n_starts = 1, max_iter = 10, seed = 1)
mmm
#> Mixed Markov Model
#>   Sequences: 30  |  Clusters: 2  |  States: 3
#>   ICs: LL = -62.330  |  BIC = 182.480  |  AIC = 158.659  |  ICL = 184.652
#>   Quality: AvePP = 0.965  |  Entropy = 0.212  |  Class.Err = 3.5%
#> 
#>   Cluster  N           Mix%   AvePP
#>   1        24 (80.0%)  78.1%  0.966
#>   2        6 (20.0%)   21.9%  0.961
# \donttest{
seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE), V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE), V4 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE)
)
mmm <- build_mmm(seqs, k = 2, seed = 42)
print(mmm)
#> Mixed Markov Model
#>   Sequences: 30  |  Clusters: 2  |  States: 3
#>   ICs: LL = -120.823  |  BIC = 299.466  |  AIC = 275.646  |  ICL = 299.990
#>   Quality: AvePP = 0.992  |  Entropy = 0.035  |  Class.Err = 0.8%
#> 
#>   Cluster  N           Mix%   AvePP
#>   1        12 (40.0%)  40.7%  0.999
#>   2        18 (60.0%)  59.3%  0.987
summary(mmm)
#> Mixed Markov Model
